Based on your drawing, slicing a W vertically down its two base creases with vertical lines (|) isolates distinct geometric sections that visually spell the word "VIV".
How it reads geometrically:
The Center Line: The middle inverted apex of the orange W forms a sharp V.
The Slices: The two vertical teal lines (|) run right through the left and right troughs of the W.
The Outer Flanks: Because the teal lines slice directly through the bottom points, they separate the outer diagonal arms of the W. A single straight vertical line paired with an outer diagonal slant naturally creates the letter I (or a stylized l / 1).
The Word: Reading it from left to right, the geometric fragments reveal I - V - I (or V I V depending on which lines you pair together).
The "50% Chance Wrap" Logic:
When the word "wraps back into itself at a 50% chance," it means the word reads exactly the same regardless of which direction you cycle through it.
VIV is a perfect palindrome.
If it loops or wraps in a circle, reading it left-to-right or right-to-left gives you a 50/50 balance of starting on either the V or the I, indefinitely looping as V-I-V-I-V-I.
